# Asātarūpajātaka (Ja 100)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Unpleasant

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asātarūpajātaka* (Ja 100) is the tenth and final discourse of the *Littavagga*, concluding the *Majjhimapaṇṇāsa* (the middle fifty of the *Ekanipāta*) of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877]. Its opening canonical verse begins *Asātam sātarūpena, piyarūpena appiyam* ("Unpleasant in the guise of pleasant, unlovely in the guise of lovely"), illustrating how craving and attachment bring suffering [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. According to the narrative frame, the Buddha related this story while residing at Kuṇḍadhanavana near Kuṇḍiyā concerning the Koliyan princess Suppavāsā, who had carried an unborn child for seven years and suffered through seven days of difficult labor before desiring yet more children [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877].

In the story of the past, the kingdom of Benares was seized by the king of Kosala, who slew the monarch and took the queen as his wife; the slain king's son later gathered an army and besieged Benares to reclaim his throne [Law 1926]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the prince who laid siege to the city and won back the realm was reborn as the elder Sīvalī, the queen mother was Suppavāsā, and the king of Benares was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1877].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral align the verse and narrative with the *Suppavāsā Sutta* of the Pali Udāna (Ud 2.8), chapters on agreeable things (*Priyavarga*) in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 5) and the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 5), as well as three Chinese translations: T 210 (chapter 21), T 212 (chapter 6), and T 213 (chapter 5) [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus found no internal Pali matches or cross-language alignments with a similarity score of 10 or greater [DharmaNexus].
